newsitem.title: UK: Branson delighted rival balloonists are safe.
newsitem.headline: Branson delighted rival balloonists are safe.

text.p: Entrepreneur Richard Branson said on Sunday he was delighted his Swiss and Belgian rivals in the race to make the first circumnavigation of the Earth by balloon had survived their latest failed attempt.
But he added that following the ditching of their Breitling Orbiter balloon in the Mediterranean on Sunday, he planned to make another attempt to accomplish the feat later this year.
Switzerland's Bertrand Piccard and Belgium's Wim Verstraeten put their balloon down in the Mediterranean just six hours after lifting off from the Swiss Alps.

The failure of their mission came four days after Branson narrowly escaped death when the balloon in which he was travelling made a dizzying descent into the Algerian desert less than 24 hours after taking off from neighbouring Morocco.

Branson was in Chateau D'Oex in Switzerland to see Piccard and Verstraeten take off, and then got into a private plane to see them flying at 30,000 feet (9,000 metres) over the Alps, before heading back to Britain.
"It was a bit strange for me being in a plane watching them after what happened just a few days previously," he told Reuters by telephone shortly after arriving back in Britain.
"I feel incredibly sorry for them after what has happened," he added. "But having been through it myself, I am delighted that they are well."
But he said that, provided no one else accomplished a circumnavigation meanwhile, he planned a further attempt later this year.
"This is very new technology. No one has flown more than 7,000 miles (11,270 km) in a balloon so far and we are trying to stretch that to 24,000 miles (38,400 km)," Branson said.
"But Piccard and Verstraeten will have learned an awful lot from this attempt just as we have learned an awful lot from ours," the British airline-to-record shop businessman said.
